newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to chair meeting on military reform.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to chair meeting on military reform.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will chair on Thursday a meeting of the Defence Council, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

The meeting, which has been postponed several times due to Yeltsin's illness, is expected to discuss military reform, one of the few areas in which changes have barely started. It also takes place one week before Yeltsin is due to sign an accord with NATO.

During his reelection campaign last summer, Yeltsin, worried by a general decline in the Russian armed forces and their enormous cost for the struggling economy, ordered the huge and largely ineffective Soviet-era force to be turned into a compact professional army by 2000.
But the reform has been stalled by rivalry between the Defence Council, an advisory board of top security officials run by his close aide Yuri Baturin, and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.
The rivals are arguing about practical ways to reform the armed forces. But both appear to agree that the deadline set by Yeltsin cannot be met.
Kremlin sources have said that Yeltsin was annoyed by the stalemate in the military reform and was preparing to intervene to get it going again.
